option.plaincraft_great_wall.bodyHint: The segment count is derived from the length; there is nothing to fill in.
Wall length in blocks. 0 means unlimited, running to the world border.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_weigh: Weight of the centre's lift over its two side samples (ridge). Positive rewards a convex crest, negative penalises it.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_promi: Weight of the centre's prominence over its 8 surrounding samples.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_slope: Weight of the height change between consecutive steps. Negative penalises steep slopes.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_turn_: Weight of the lateral-offset change (turning). Negative penalises sharp turns.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_wet_w: Weight applied when the centre column is water or upper-censored. Negative penalises water.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_depar: Weight of departure from the anchor centre line. Negative penalises drift.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.summit_flat: A centre lift at or below this many blocks is a flat summit (walkable, rewarded); above it is a knife ridge (penalised).
Reward for a flat summit (small lift). Positive encourages walking the summit.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.knife_ridge: Penalty for a knife ridge (large lift). Negative avoids very narrow ridges.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_asymm: Penalty for the height difference between the two side samples (a slope). Negative avoids a side-slope.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.ridge_accum: Penalty for continuous climbing. Negative avoids a wall that climbs steadily uphill.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.obstacle_ma: The centre line treats a structure footprint within this distance as an obstacle. Larger detours further.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.fine_sample: Default 1, i.e. 1000 drives per second. The fine sample used to have no dedicated driver at all and ran on server ticks (about 20/s), which left one measured session unable to finish a single slice in 27 minutes. Raising this lowers sampling throughput proportionally; use it only to yield CPU to other mods.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.lane_batch_: Default 256, and 256 is also the ceiling: the sampling contracts require a single grant to fall in 1..256 and throw otherwise, so the value here is clamped automatically.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.chunk_cache: Default 16. Baked chunks are cached by construction origin, and a hit skips the whole bake. One cross-section sweep hits about 13 cells, so a smaller value starts thrashing; a larger one costs heap in proportion.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.fine_step.t: Default 2. 1 disables thinning entirely and matches the old behaviour; 2 probes every other flank column. The centre band and both edges are always probed column by column, so thinning never reaches the wall body; a column that is not probed takes the maximum of its two probed neighbours (fill dirt, never cut rock). Note that a fill cannot see a feature narrower than the stride: a one-block spike or pond between two probed columns is invisible, so a larger stride widens that blind spot on the flanks.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.steep_thres: Default 3. When two probed columns differ by at least this much, every column between them is probed too, because that is where a foundation changes level. Lower is more conservative and slower.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.core_half_w: Default 12. Columns within this distance of the centre are always probed one by one and never thinned. 24 means fully unthinned (most conservative); lowering it saves more columns but leaves the wall body relying on fills.
config.plaincraft_great_wall.refine_wate: Default on. When any probed column reports water, the whole cross-section escalates to full resolution and the escalation carries to the next route point, so a water body cannot end between two points. Water cannot be synthesised the way a height can: guessing land makes the wall run through the water, guessing water makes the assembly skip those blocks and leaves holes in the wall. Turning it off is faster but a narrow water strip can be filled as land.
